Resolve the selected task with `pose context --task <typed-or-qualified-artifact-ref> --json` before reviewing. Follow its canonical authority and stop on ambiguity, stale binding, unsupported metadata or `transfer-in-progress`. Use the qualified `xref:` scope for cross-project review; every cross-project write requires an explicit `POSE_PROJECT_ROOTS` binding and the current `context_revision` as `--expect-context`. Keep review evidence and its `POSE-Spec:` trailer in the authority repository.

## Steps

1. Classify the change as feature, bugfix, refactor, documentation, or mixed.
2. Run `pose assess tech-debt` during code review to ensure markers (`TODO`, `FIXME`, `stub`, `panic`) are covered by follow-ups or specs. Run `pose assess integrate` when touching inter-module contracts (Protobuf, Kafka, REST, MCP).
3. Resolve `pose review bundle <scope> --explain` to inspect effective criteria, components and tool requirements.
4. Run active required tools first, record why each recommended tool was used or skipped, and keep completion tools deferred until attestation.
5. Select rules with `pose suggest review --path <affected-dir>` for every mapped component.
6. Search `.pose/knowledge/` for prior module decisions, accepted risks, and pending follow-ups.
7. Require deterministic `pose validate --strict` evidence matching delivery targets.
8. Evaluate every required plan criterion, including cross-component boundaries. When the change adds or alters a governance gate, also answer: what is the cheapest way to satisfy this gate in form without producing its value, and what stops that? Point to the adversarial corpus case that proves it (`pose-mcp/internal/cli/testdata/adversarial/README.md`), or record the gap.
9. Classify findings as critical, high, medium, or low with evidence and expected action.
10. Run `pose recurrence-check --tolerant --window-days 14`; use recurrence escalation for a matching systemic signal.
11. Create a handoff with `pose new-knowledge handoff <slug>` for accepted residual risk, monitoring, or deferred action.
12. Seal the review subject with `pose review bundle <scope> --seal`.
13. Prepare the mechanical half with `pose review auto-attest <bundle-id> --reviewer agent:<id>` — without `--apply` — and read `review_attestation.pending`: those are the criteria no registered check answers, and they are yours to answer. Then record the attestation with `pose review attest`, giving every judgment criterion a conclusion. `--apply` on auto-attest records only when nothing is pending; it refuses otherwise, and never answers a judgment criterion for you. An explicit attestation records `--criterion ID|passed|evidence` (or `not-applicable` with a rationale, or `finding` naming a recorded finding) and `--finding ID|severity|disposition|action|evidence[|owner|rationale|review-by]`; every finding needs a severity and an action, and an `accepted-risk` or `wont-fix` finding also needs an owner, a rationale and a review date. A `passed` criterion may cite only evidence the sealed bundle contains, of a class the criterion accepts. For a cross-project attestation, use the qualified `xref:` as the target argument to `pose review attest`, include `--expect-context <digest>` with `--apply`, and keep the explicit project binding; a bundle ID alone does not select an authority project.
14. Run `pose review verify <scope>` and `pose review-check <scope>`; close only when both confirm a valid, approved attestation.
15. Decide: approved, approved with reservations, changes requested, or rejected.
16. When Contributor Mode is active, if review uncovers POSE linter false-positives, diagnostic frictions, or rule gaps, stage an improvement proposal with `pose contribute stage --type enhancement --title "<summary>"`.

## Output requirements

- Completed Rules applied during review section.
- Bundle/plan digests and dispositions for required, recommended and deferred completion tools.
- Severity-classified findings with expected actions.
- Clear and actionable final decision.
- Handoff when residual risk is accepted.

… k; agora só a falta de repositório ou de commit em HEAD o suprime, e as demais falhas viram `warn` com a descrição limitada (`TestDoctorCommitGraphReportsAnUnreadableHistory`, com um commit pai apagado).

Rodada 2 (run rrn-c7c3feb56ea14783, recusada porque os ids dos achados novos traziam o prefixo de rodada `R2-`; o rascunho declarou F2 a F4 corrigidos e F5 parcial). Os achados, corrigidos com teste que reprova sem a correção: F6 qualquer falha do primeiro `rev-parse` era tratada como "não se aplica"; agora só um diretório que não é repositório (`rev-parse --git-dir` com a mensagem do Git, lida no locale C) e um HEAD que não resolve (saída 1 de `rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD`) suprimem o check, e um HEAD cujo commit não pode ser lido, ou um repositório que o Git não abre, é `warn` (`TestDoctorCommitGraphTellsUnbornFromBroken`). F7 o caminho sondado era lido como pathspec, e um nome como `*` mudava a busca; agora a busca roda com `GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1` (`TestDoctorCommitGraphProbesALiteralPath`). F8 com `core.commitGraph=false`, `commitGraph.readChangedPaths=false` ou `commitGraph.changedPathsVersion=0`, reescrever o grafo não mudava a resposta; agora o `doctor` reporta `git.commit-graph-reads` em `warn`, sem correção automática, nomeando a configuração, e não recomenda reescrever o grafo (`TestDoctorCommitGraphNamesDisabledReads`).

Rodada 5 (run rrn-6d639d1e28201081, changes-requested; as rodadas 3 e 4 falharam na limpeza do worktree pelo teto de 256 MiB, mas a 3 registrou F9 a F14). Seis bloqueadores, F15 a F20, que reabrem F9 a F14, corrigidos com teste que reprova sem a correção. F15 um clone raso, em que o Git não usa nem escreve commit-graph, recebia uma correção que não resolve; agora não se aplica (`TestDoctorCommitGraphSkipsAShallowClone`). F16 a correção herdava `commitGraph.maxNewFilters`; agora passa `--max-new-filters=-1` (`TestDoctorCommitGraphFixIgnoresMaxNewFilters`). F17 uma árvore de HEAD vazia recomendava reescrever para sempre; agora não se aplica (`TestDoctorCommitGraphSkipsAnEmptyTree`). F18 `readChangedPaths` era lido antes de `changedPathsVersion`, que o Git trata como prioritário; a ordem segue o Git (`TestDoctorCommitGraphFollowsConfigurationPrecedence`). F19 os comandos de diagnóstico podiam buscar objetos num clone parcial; agora rodam com `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, e a falta de objetos vira `warn` sem contato com o remoto (`TestDoctorCommitGraphNeverFetches`, que conta os objetos antes e depois). F20 o stderr de um comando bem-sucedido era descartado, e um commit-graph ilegível, que o Git anuncia e contorna, virava recomendação; agora é `warn` com a mensagem do Git (`TestDoctorCommitGraphReportsAnUnreadableGraph`).

Rodada 6 (run rrn-f159474ba8bf6bc9, changes-requested): F9, F10, F12, F13, F15, F16, F18 e F19 corrigidos; três bloqueadores restantes, corrigidos com teste que reprova sem a correção. F21 abaixo do limite de 500 commits, o stderr do `rev-list` bem-sucedido era descartado e um commit-graph ilegível virava `ok`; agora o aviso do Git vira `warn` em qualquer tamanho de histórico (`TestDoctorCommitGraphWarnsBelowTheThreshold`). F22 a exclusão da árvore vazia vinha depois do retorno do histórico curto; agora vem antes (`TestDoctorCommitGraphSkipsAShortEmptyTree`). F23 o comando exibido omitia `--max-new-filters=-1`; agora a dica e a descrição da correção mostram `commitGraphWriteCommand`, o mesmo comando que a correção roda, e seguir a dica à mão sob `commitGraph.maxNewFilters=0` grava os filtros (`TestDoctorCommitGraphShowsTheEffectiveCommand`).

Rodada 7 (run rrn-5e598ead031d2345, changes-requested): F24 `commitGraph.changedPathsVersion` com um valor que o Git não suporta (por exemplo 3) faz o Git não ler filtro nenhum, e o `doctor` recomendava reescrever o grafo, o que mantém a configuração. Agora só -1, 1 e 2 contam como leitura habilitada; 0 e qualquer valor fora disso viram `git.commit-graph-reads` em `warn`, nomeando a configuração (`TestDoctorCommitGraphNamesAnUnsupportedVersion`, que reprova sem a correção).
